title: Craniofacial characteristics on the lateral cephalometric radiograph in obstructive sleep apnea compared to healthy controls
summary: This prospective clinical study investigates whether there are differences in the width of the upper airway in the posterior pharyngeal region between patients with and without obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) that are visible on lateral X-ray images. It will also examine whether other facial and cranial features can be identified in patients with OSA.

interventions.name:
Patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA positive group)

Measurements are taken from the available lateral cephalometric radiographs (measurements of the posterior upper airway, the position of the hyoid bone, and the skeletal relationship of the maxilla and the mandible, the vertical skeletal
Patients without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA negative group)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
OSA positive group: AHI ≥ 5
OSA negative group: AHI < 5
Lateral cephalometric radiograph taken based on a justified indication
Exclusion criteria:
No consent to participate in the study
No consent to receive information about incidental findings (e.g., sleep apnea, other sleep abnormalities)
Presence of craniofacial syndromes
History of severe accidents involving fractures in the facial skull or cervical spine
